## Abstract

Off-budget fiscal schemes can obscure public liabilities and complicate the enforcement of fiscal rules. We develop a signalling model in which a government privately knows its type and chooses whether to report borrowing transparently or conceal it, while the European Commission decides whether to impose sanctions. A two-period extension shows how weak enforcement and severe sanctions can encourage concealment even by a responsible government. A two-country extension examines how debt preferences and unequal bargaining power shape cooperation under proportional and fixed penalties.

## About this work

Joint work with **Henrik Berger, Sara Feore, and Lauri Hannikainen**. The analysis uses Italy’s Superbonus policy to explore the incentives created by fiscal rules and their enforcement.
